name: dTRINITY dUSD
oneLiner: dUSD is dTRINITY's USD stablecoin minted 1:1 against yield-bearing reserve stablecoins, with Curve AMOs and stability operations defending the peg.
collateral: Ethereum: USDT0/USDC0-style whitelisted stablecoin and yield-bearing collateral in isolated dUSD reserves. Fraxtal: frxUSD/sfrxUSD and other Frax-aligned USD collateral in isolated reserves. Katana: whitelisted USD stablecoins and yieldcoins in isolated reserves. Sonic: whitelisted USD stablecoins/yieldcoins such as frxUSD/sfrxUSD in isolated reserves. Each network deployment maintains fully isolated reserves with no cross-chain collateral sharing.
pegMechanism: Atomic 1:1 mint (no fee) and redemption (up to 50 bps fee) against whitelisted reserve stablecoins; Algorithmic Market Operations (AMO) pre-mint dUSD into Curve liquidity pools to programmatically support the peg; Stability Market Operations (SMO) buy back and burn dUSD from Curve when it trades at a significant discount; dUSD price is hard-coded at $1 in all protocol-internal operations to prevent oracle manipulation.

oracleRisk.summary: dUSD's own price is hard-coded at $1 for mint, redeem, and dLEND lending/borrowing to resist manipulation, but the protocol values its yield-bearing reserve stablecoins (e.g. sfrxUSD, sUSDS) and dLEND collateral through external feeds — API3 and Redstone, with Chainlink and issuer feeds — and those feeds drive reserve NAV and mint/redeem ratios. No documented single-primary-with-failover oracle architecture per asset.

branchApplicability.rationale: dUSD is minted and redeemed against protocol reserves, while dLEND separately values borrower collateral and manages liquidations. dUSD itself is disabled as dLEND collateral and is not a borrower-owned debt position with token-level liquidation branches, so the CDP branch inventory is not applicable; reserve and lending oracle dependencies remain captured in the profile summary.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: dTRINITY is chain-isolated by design: dUSD on Ethereum, Sonic, Katana, and Fraxtal are separately-issued non-fungible deployments, each administered by dTRINITY's own governance (1-day timelocked 3-of-5 Safes on Ethereum/Katana/Fraxtal; direct 3-of-5 Safe on Sonic). No third-party bridge controls dUSD minting anywhere.

routes.reviewNote: Issuer-native deployment: dTRINITY is chain-isolated by design ('dTRINITY intentionally sacrifices cross-chain fungibility'); the Ethereum dUSD is administered by the 1-day TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE verified 2026-07-20) behind the 3-of-5 Timelocked Governance Safe 0xE83c188a7BE46B90715C757A06cF917175f30262, with minting through the AMO Manager 0x29532F74A9302e0a1E9f7d015FE355FFdE6e6880 (MINTER_ROLE verified).

Issuer-native deployment (chain-isolated architecture): the Fraxtal dUSD proxy is administered by the Fraxtal 1-day TimelockController 0x0bafada2a5824864720873ee40cd960b36445212 behind the Fraxtal 3-of-5 Governance Safe 0xfC2f89F9982BE98A9672CEFc3Ea6dBBdd88bc8e9 (role reads 2026-07-20).

Issuer-native deployment (chain-isolated architecture): the Katana dUSD proxy is administered by the 1-day TimelockController at the same address as Ethereum 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b behind the 3-of-5 Governance Safe (role reads 2026-07-20).

Issuer-native deployment (chain-isolated architecture): the Sonic dUSD proxy is administered directly by the 3-of-5 Governance Safe 0xE83c188a7BE46B90715C757A06cF917175f30262 with no timelock (role reads 2026-07-20) — a weaker control than the other chains, and the deployment is absent from dTRINITY's docs registry (flagged).

applicabilityBasis.summary: dUSD is a DeFi-native, crypto-collateralized stablecoin issued by a Singapore-domiciled non-profit foundation (Trinity Foundation Ltd.) that explicitly restricts US persons from accessing the protocol; GENIUS Act scope over foreign DeFi issuers with a US geo-block is legally uncertain, so applicability remains unclear rather than definitively in or out of scope.

genius.notes: Issuer is Trinity Foundation Ltd., a Singapore non-profit public company limited by guarantee (ACRA UEN 202414739E, registered 2024-04-15); it states it does not control or operate dTRINITY on any blockchain. US persons are explicitly excluded from the protocol (Restricted Regions page lists United States). Note: Singapore is also listed as a restricted jurisdiction, though the foundation is domiciled there — this reflects the protocol's legal distancing from the foundation entity. Terms of Use are governed by Cayman Islands law. GENIUS Act applicability to a foreign non-profit foundation operating a permissionless DeFi protocol with a US geo-block is legally unresolved; no PPSI approval or issuer pathway was identified.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: dTRINITY documentation describes dUSD as a protocol stablecoin with whitelisted stablecoin and yield-bearing collateral, while the reviewed Ethereum mint-control record identifies a proxy and unresolved AMO/SMO controller identity. The reserve policy can include issuer-controlled stablecoins, but no deployment-wide holder blacklist or freeze function is proven in the reviewed sources; inherited upstream exposure and unresolved control reach are retained.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: dUSD minting on Ethereum runs through the AMO Manager and one additional undocumented minter contract under a 1-day timelocked 3-of-5 Governance Safe; a separate 5-of-5 Emergency Safe holds pause only. Deployments are chain-isolated; Sonic is administered by the Governance Safe directly without a timelock.

controls.label: dTRINITY AMO Manager (peg operations controller)
controls.evidence: The docs-registry AMO Manager holds MINTER_ROLE on the Ethereum dUSD token (hasRole = true, re-verified 2026-07-20; RoleGranted event at block 23987067). It mints dUSD directly for algorithmic market operations against the Collateral Vault 0x84c58066a4408454b7380f168c95F571419253f4. Note: dTRINITY's registry documents an AMO only — no separate 'SMO' controller exists.

controls.label: dTRINITY second MINTER_ROLE holder (undocumented in registry)
controls.evidence: A second contract (5,738 bytes of code) holds MINTER_ROLE on the Ethereum dUSD token (hasRole = true, re-verified 2026-07-20; granted by event at block 23983666). It is not listed in dTRINITY's docs contract registry (flagged); its function is otherwise unidentified, but its mint capability is live and identical in kind to the AMO Manager's.

controls.label: dTRINITY Timelocked Governance 3-of-5 Safe (1-day TimelockController)
controls.evidence: dUSD DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is held by the OZ v5 TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b (getMinDelay() = 86,400 s; hasRole verified 2026-07-20) whose sole proposer and executor is this 3-of-5 Safe (owners read on-chain). Through the timelock the Safe can grant/revoke MINTER_ROLE and administer the dUSD proxy-admin chain. On Sonic the same Safe holds DEFAULT_ADMIN directly with no timelock (flagged).

controls.label: dTRINITY Emergency Governance 5-of-5 Safe (PAUSER_ROLE)
controls.evidence: This 5-of-5 Safe (owners read on-chain 2026-07-20) holds PAUSER_ROLE on the Ethereum dUSD token (granted at block 25112809; hasRole re-verified 2026-07-20) — emergency pause only, no mint or admin capability.

review.evidence: ETH block 25295164: dUSD is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy; ProxyAdmin (0xbe90db...) owner is an OZ TimelockController (0x18cb0e...) with 24h delay and no active proposers (0 RoleGranted events, all hasRole checks returned false). Upgrade path is effectively locked. Sonic: proxy admin owner is a 2/3 multisig (0xE83C18..., 3 owners, threshold 2 via getThreshold). AMO/SMO contract addresses not resolvable from known contract addresses — contributor mint admin identity on ETH remains unconfirmed. 2026-07-20 (Kimi P2 dc-2): AMO Manager 0x29532F74A9302e0a1E9f7d015FE355FFdE6e6880 (docs registry) and a second, registry-undocumented minter 0xf84cc8217713a53fc3e3eb2d62d2af33a084ff85 both hold MINTER_ROLE on the Ethereum dUSD token (hasRole reads). DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE sits with the 1-day TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b behind the 3-of-5 Governance Safe 0xE83c188a7BE46B90715C757A06cF917175f30262 (owners read). Emergency pause rests with the 5-of-5 Safe 0x04401537CA997a43EBCFEc8194c7e88c7ee79804. dTRINITY is chain-isolated by design; Sonic uses a direct Safe admin with no timelock and is absent from the docs registry.
